messages:
mara: Heads-up — acme-prod p99 token-gen latency spiked in eu-west-1, jumped from ~110ms to ~900ms around 09:12 UTC. Traces show some requests egressing to us-west-2. Anyone on this?
ingrid: seeing it too for a handful of tenants in the same AZ. started ~09:10-09:15.
sre-oncall: i'm on it, can you paste a trace id?
mara: trace id 0a1b2c9f. Sample span path below (from tracing UI):
```
client -> frontend-eu-west-1 -> ingress-proxy-eu -> smart-router -> egress-node-us-west-2 -> model-server-us-west-2
```
josh: :eyes: that's an unexpected hop. smart-router should prefer local egress pools for eu requests. wonder if the eu pool drained for that customer.
alex: checking egress-pool metrics, eu-west-1 pool for reserved-dedicated instances shows healthy but utilization jumped a bit. there was a control-plane push at 09:08 that updated fallback policy for several tenants.
mara: ah — support ticket mentioned a routing policy tweak by platform-tools this morning. could be collateral.
support-bot: Deployment event: platform-tools/routing-policy v3.12 -> applied @ 09:07 UTC to customer-groups:{acme,globex} (change id rp-2025-0411)
ingrid: can someone query the router decision logs for that trace id?
sre-oncall: running quick grep on router logs: `kubectl logs router-7b9c -n infra | grep 0a1b2c9f -A3` yields: 
```
2025-04-11T09:11:26Z router[info] trace=0a1b2c9f decision: fallback_policy=global_low_cost matched, pick_pool=us-west-2, reason=cost_threshold
2025-04-11T09:11:26Z router[debug] pool_weights: eu-west-1=0.6, us-west-2=0.4, reserved_pools_down=[]
```
alex: that log line makes it look like the new policy allowed global_low_cost to take precedence for some requests, despite region affinity. maybe a bug in policy evaluation ordering.
josh: can we repro with a synthetic request? I can hit the routing debug endpoint: `/routing/debug?tenant=acme&trace=manual-1`
josh: result: picks us-west-2 for ~30% of requests when header `X-Prefer-Local` missing. If header present, stays in eu.
mara: most SDKs don't set X-Prefer-Local by default — our client lib relies on router defaulting to local. So this change could explain wide impact.
sre-oncall: mitigation: rolling back rp-2025-0411 now. also pushing a hotfix to routing evaluation to ensure region_affinity outranks cost-based fallback for dedicated tenants.
dev-bot: rollback started: platform-tools/routing-policy rp-2025-0411 -> rollback in progress (job 98765)
support-bot: Alert cleared? any telemetry?
alex: after rollback, re-running traces for same request ids shows egress back to eu nodes. p99 for acme-prod dropped back to ~130ms within 4 mins.
mara: confirmed from customer dashboard — latency back to normal.
ingrid: filing follow-up: create a test that asserts region_affinity precedence and add canary gate to routing policy changes.
josh: logging a ticket to add a client-side header `X-Prefer-Local: true` in our SDK for critical tenants as a belt-and-suspenders approach.
sre-oncall: note for postmortem: change id rp-2025-0411 lacked sufficient canary for routing semantics. no infra outage but severe latency impact for reserved customers.
mara: thanks all. marking this thread resolved — will open a postmortem and CC platform-tools and client-sdk teams. :thumbsup:
sre-oncall: adding action items to incident board. :white_check_mark:
